title: IBM's Bee AI framework in three facts
oneliner: IBM's Bee framework runs many small specialized AI agents like a bee colony - swarm intelligence, with each agent doing one task toward a shared goal, and it is energy efficient.
says: Three facts about IBM's Bee agentic framework: it is inspired by nature, specifically honeybee colonies where each bee handles one task toward the colony's goal - in Bee, many small agents each take a particular task to achieve a global one. It uses swarm intelligence, the same principle as ant colonies and bird flocks: individuals follow local rules, and the group accomplishes the large task together. And it is energy efficient compared to monolithic approaches.
explained: This reel captures a design philosophy that later runs through his whole platform series: many small, single-purpose agents beat one giant do-everything model. A monolithic agent is hard to test, hard to debug, and fails opaquely. A swarm of narrow agents is composable - each one is simple enough to verify, and the system's intelligence comes from how they are coordinated.

Swarm intelligence is the coordination pattern: no central puppet-master (no single system controlling everything), just agents following local rules and passing work along. The energy-efficiency claim follows from the same idea - small specialized components can run smaller models for their narrow task instead of invoking a frontier model for everything. That trade-off, cost and energy versus capability per task, becomes a recurring theme in his inference-economics reels.
takeaway: Agent architecture mirrors good software architecture: small, single-purpose components with clear coordination beat one opaque monolith.
